rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.4 and 3 - the study uses a four-year Bushland, TX field experiment (MESA, LESA, LEPA, SDI at 0-100% ET replacement) to drive multivariate empirical yield/price simulations validated against the field observations (Table 1, Table 2), then runs an enterprise budget and SERF risk analysis of net returns (Figs. 4-9).
rows.notes: The study contains nothing about metered power connections or electricity metering; it is a Texas High Plains economic risk analysis of four irrigation systems and ET-replacement levels. Its own results concern net returns and certainty equivalents: SDI gave the highest lint yield at each level and a similar net return at 75% and 100% ET replacement, so the authors infer SDI 'could potentially save irrigation water' at 75% ET without loss of profit (Sections 3.4, 4). Irrigation amounts were experimental treatments, not an observed outcome of adoption, and groundwater extraction reduction conditional on metering was never examined. The passage's specific claim (reduction in groundwater extraction only when power is metered) is not supported by this study; the technology (SDI) matches but the effect and its condition do not.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). The study is a primary economic-simulation analysis built on field data; the review's attribution of a metering condition to this paper appears to be a misattribution, likely belonging to Bahinipati & Viswanathan 2019.
